headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Sure! If you’re looking for a ready‑made API that accepts an IP address and returns company‑level data (including contact details when available), here are a few popular options you can consider: | Service | Key Features | Typical Data Returned | Pricing (as of 2026) | |---------|--------------|-----------------------|----------------------| | **IPinfo.io** | • IP geolocation, ASN, carrier, and company info
• Optional “company” endpoint for business data
• Free tier (50k requests/month) | • Company name, domain, industry, size, logo, contact email (if public)
• ASN, organization, country, city, postal code | • Free tier: 50k/month
• Paid plans start at $5/month (200k requests) | | **ipdata.co** | • IP geolocation + company lookup via “company” endpoint
• Includes domain, industry, revenue, employee count, and contact email | • Company name, domain, industry, revenue range, employee count, logo, contact email (if available) | • Free tier: 50k/month
• Paid plans start at $9/month (200k requests) | | **ipstack.com** | • IP geolocation + “business” endpoint for company data
• Returns company name, domain, industry, and contact email | • Company name, domain, industry, revenue, employee count, logo, contact email | • Free tier: 10k/month
• Paid plans start at $10/month (200k requests) | | **Clearbit Enrichment** | • Enriches IPs with company data via “Enrichment” API
• Returns company name, domain, industry, size, logo, and contact email (if public) | • Company name, domain, industry, employee count, logo, contact email | • Paid plans start at $99/month (200k requests) | | **Hunter.io Domain Search** | • Not IP‑based, but you can first resolve the domain via IPinfo/ipstack, then use Hunter to get emails | • Company domain, email patterns, verified emails | • Free tier: 50 emails/month
• Paid plans start at $49/month (500 emails) | ### How to Use (Example with IPinfo) ```python import requests ip = "8.8.8.8" # Example IP api_key = "YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN" # Basic IP lookup resp = requests.get(f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json?token={api_key}") data = resp.json() print(data) # Company lookup (requires paid plan) resp = requests.get(f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/company?token={api_key}") company_data = resp.json() print(company_data) ``` ### Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Accuracy** – Company data is often derived from public sources (WHOIS, LinkedIn, Crunchbase). Accuracy can vary, especially for newer or smaller companies. 2. **Privacy** – Some services may not return contact emails if they’re not publicly available or if the company has opted out of public listings. 3. **Rate Limits** – Free tiers are usually limited to 10–50k requests/month. If you need higher volume, consider a paid plan or a dedicated enterprise solution. 4. **Compliance** – Make sure you’re compliant with GDPR/CCPA when storing or using personal data (e.g., contact emails). ### Next Steps 1. **Sign up** for a free trial on one of the services above (most offer a generous free tier). 2. **Test** the API with a few IPs to see how much company data is returned and how accurate it is for your target audience. 3. **Integrate** the chosen API into your application, handling pagination and rate‑limit errors gracefully.
